title: KVCache eviction score decay and stale TTL remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
incident_summary: A production regression in the KVCache eviction scoring logic caused accelerated score decay and premature eviction of hot prefix entries. The regression increased cache miss rates during normal traffic patterns, leading to a 12-25% tail latency regression for token generation on affected hosts and elevated CPU usage from repeated KV rebuilds.
timeline:
2026-02-19 02:11 UTC - Pager triggered: elevated 99th percentile latency for generation service.
2026-02-19 02:17 UTC - On-call rotated and began triage; initial mitigation applied (throttle background sweeper).
2026-02-19 03:05 UTC - Engineering identified correlated spike in cache eviction rate and drop in per-prefix hit ratio.
2026-02-19 04:22 UTC - Quick rollback of recent runtime param change (decay constant) reduced eviction rate; latency began to normalize.
2026-02-20 to 2026-02-24 - Post-incident investigation and reproduction tests run in staging; root cause narrowed to scoring half-life change in PR #3421.
2026-02-25 - This follow-up ticket opened to track action items and remediation plan.
root_cause: A performance optimization PR modified the eviction score decay constant and TTL reconciliation path to prefer score-weighted eviction aggressively. The new decay parameter reduced score persistence for recently used prefixes (half-life decreased from 30 minutes to ~90 seconds), causing hot entries to be treated as cold under normal access patterns. Additionally, a logic regression allowed stale TTLs to be ignored when a prefix was reinserted during eviction storms, which prevented expected re-promotion behavior.
impact:
- 12-25% increase in 99th percentile generation latency on ~20% of serving hosts for ~2 hours.
- Elevated CPU and network due to repeated KV loads and cache repopulation.
- Three customer-facing errors reported (requests timed out and retried).
- No data loss or consistency violations observed.
detection: Alerting from SLO monitors (generation_99p_latency) and newly added eviction-rate telemetry surfaced the anomaly. Correlation with cache hit/miss dashboards and host-level flamegraphs pointed to repeated prefix rebuild activity. The regression was reproducible using a synthetic workload that matches prefix hot-spot skew.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back the PR that changed decay constants and disabled the aggressive TTL-skip path. Temporarily increased cache size on affected fleets and limited sweeper concurrency to reduce eviction storms. Customers on Dedicated with incidents were contacted and informed of rollback; no config changes required from customers.
long_term_actions: Add automated unit + integration tests for eviction score stability across time(series): ensure score half-life changes are within guarded bounds - owner: Liam Chen - due: 2026-03-12
Introduce canary runtime flag to gate decay parameter rollout (boolean flag + graduated ramp) and require telemetry pass before fleet-wide promotion - owner: Priya Rao - due: 2026-03-18

Implement prefix-level eviction backoff: when a prefix is evicted and reinserted within X seconds, temporarily protect it from subsequent evictions (configurable window) - owner: Marco Silva - due: 2026-03-22
Add a guardrail that caps per-host eviction rate and triggers automatic slowdown of sweeper/decay when memory pressure is low - owner: Kira Novak - due: 2026-03-15

Add end-to-end regression test in CI that runs skewed synthetic workloads to detect premature eviction under realistic access patterns before any runtime param merge - owner: SRE team - due: 2026-03-10

Improve telemetry: emit per-prefix eviction_count, last_reinsert_ts, score_value, and a synthesized 'premature_eviction' signal for easier SLO correlation - owner: Observability team - due: 2026-03-08
Backfill post-incident dashboard and runbook steps into the KVCache runbook with explicit rollback and triage checklist - owner: Aisha Patel - due: 2026-03-05
verification_plan:
1) Unit/integration tests for score decay must pass in CI for at least 48h under synthetic skewed loads.
2) Deploy canary flag to 5% of fleet; monitor per-prefix eviction_count and generation_99p_latency for 72 hours.
3) If metrics stable, increase canary to 25% and run another 72-hour window; only then promote to 100%.
4) Execute post-deployment chaos test (simulated memory pressure) to validate guardrails.
5) Close ticket after 7 days of stable telemetry at 100% rollout.
